text:
Tampa Bay arrives in Utah on the second night of a back-to-back, still stinging from a 6-3 loss at COL that ended its three-game winning streak. The Lightning are 3-2-0 in their last five and close a road trip tonight. UTA is also 3-2-0 over its last five, but it lost 5-3 at SEA two days ago, and it's playing without Michael Carcone. John Marino is day-to-day and could return.

The teams match up closely. At five on five, each has taken 58% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in its games, and the model has the game at 3.16 goals for TBL and 3.11 for UTA. The gap is on the power play: UTA creates 0.82 expected goals a game with the man advantage to TBL's 0.66, and it takes 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents chances too.

In net, projected starter Karel Vejmelka (UTA) is 3.4 goals worse than expected this season, though he was 5.4 better last year. Projected Lightning starter Dennis Hildeby is 0.8 better than expected in two games and was 10.1 better in 20 games last season. Backup Hildeby starts over Andrei Vasilevskiy.

Watch Brandon Hagel, on a four-game point streak and given a 42% chance to score, and Nikita Kucherov, at 79% to record a point. For UTA, Dylan Guenther has a 33% chance to score, and Clayton Keller is at 69% for a point.
